summary: Filippo Marsili works in sinology and history/archaeology. He completed graduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley (~2002–2009) under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, Arcangela Santoro, and Paolo Daffinà. He held a post at Saint Louis University around 2011.

Finnian M. M. Gerety is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his doctorate from Harvard University (~2008–2015). He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Yale University (2017–2018) and served as a visiting assistant professor at Brown University (~2016–2019).

Fitzedward Hall (1825–1901) was an Indologist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (~1840–1842) and Harvard University (~1842–1846). He held academic posts at Benares Sanskrit College (~1850–1855) and King's College London (~1862–1869).

Flavio A. Geisshuesler specializes in Tibetology and religious studies, having studied at the universities of Lausanne, Bern, and Virginia (PhD ~2014–2020), as well as under Dan Martin. He was a postdoctoral researcher at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2019.

Florin Deleanu works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg (PhD 1998–2005). He held posts at Waseda, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Kansai Medical University.
Florinda De Simini is an Indologist who has held posts at the University of Naples Federico II and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2017).

Francesco Sferra is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Raffaele Torella and Raniero Gnoli. He has held posts at the Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente, Series Minor, University of Naples "L'Orientale", and University of Naples Federico II.

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton (1762–1829) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1780–1783). He served in the Indian Medical Service (~1794–1815) and succeeded Henry Thomas Colebrooke in 1814.

Francis Gladwin (1745–1812) was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was a founding member of the Asiatic Society in 1784 and became a professor of Persian at Fort William College in 1800.

Francis H. Cook is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed doctoral work at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970). He served as an emeritus professor at UC Riverside (~1970–1994) and became chair at the Numata Center in 1999.

Francis N. J. is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed a master's degree in ancient history and doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier at the University of Calicut until 2002.
Francis Robinson is a historian of religion and Indology who attended Bexhill College. Around 1973, he became a professor at Royal Holloway, University of London.

Francis Tiso is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Cornell University (~1968–1972), Harvard Divinity School (~1972–1974), and Columbia University (~1975–1989).

Francis Woodman Cleaves (1911–1995) was a sinologist, linguist, and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1937–1942) and subsequently held a post there from ~1946 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Fordham and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1979–1984), he has held posts at Boston College, the University of Oxford, the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies, and Harvard University.

Francisco García Ayuso (1845–1897) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Martin Haug at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from ~1869 to 1872.

Francisco Varela (1946–2001) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Chile and Harvard. He founded the Mind & Life Institute and held posts at the University of Chile, Naropa University, École Polytechnique, and CNRS.

Franciscus Verellen is a sinologist and historian educated at Hamburg, Oxford, and the EPHE under Kristofer Schipper. He has held posts at the EFEO, Princeton University, the Institute for Advanced Study, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Frank J. Hoffman works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaii (~1976–1978) under teachers including Eliot Deutsch and David J. Kalupahana, completing his doctorate (~1978–1981) under Stewart Sutherland and Richard Gombrich.

Frank Raymond Allchin (1923–2010) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of London (~1947–1954). He held posts at SOAS, the University of Cambridge, and the Ancient India and Iran Trust, and founded EASAA in 1970.
